title: After the August 2021 fire, finding an almost twin Aronde again
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The August 2021 fire interrupted a very concrete story. Looking for another Aronde was not a way to deny the loss, but to recover a possible continuity.
content:
In August 2021, our first Simca Aronde disappeared in a fire. What such an event first breaks is often the ordinary life around the car: trips, habits and the familiar presence of the machine, more than its material value alone.

Losing a car that belonged to daily life

A classic car is never only an object in storage. When it truly runs, it organises departures, stops, visits and a family rhythm. The August 2021 fire broke that in a single moment, with the very concrete sense of emptiness many collectors know.

The memory of the model remains, but its texture changes. One then has to accept that the story of the first car stops there, without trying to replace it bolt for bolt.

Looking for a twin without chasing an illusion

When we speak of an almost twin Aronde, we do not mean an exact double. We mean a car that brings back the same family of sensations: driving position, engine rhythm, the plain reading of the saloon and the calm presence an Aronde keeps on the roads of the gulf.

That nuance leads to a sounder purchase. Instead of rebuilding the past, one chooses a car able to open a credible next chapter.

What the second car truly changes

The second Aronde does not replace the first one. It allows the thread to be taken up again. The gestures return, and so do the routes, with another car but within the same setting of life and attachment.

This may be the clearest way to understand a collector car when it is really lived with. Its value does not rest on rarity alone. It rests on the concrete place it can take back inside ordinary time.

This note extends the page our Simca Aronde A90 Elysee in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez. Within the same cluster, the next useful step is Buying a second Simca Aronde A90 Elysee in spring 2022.
